domain_context: Free-text entries from public clinical trial documentation.

paths.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the heart, blood vessels, and circulation (e.g., Myocardial Infarction, Arrhythmia, Heart Failure). Excludes baseline cardiovascular conditions.
Events involving coronary blood flow reduction or heart muscle death (e.g., MI, Ischemia, Angina, Occlusion).
Electrical disturbances affecting heart rate or rhythm (e.g., SVT, Atrial Fibrillation, Bradycardia, Tachycardia).
Issues affecting blood vessel integrity, patency, or devices (e.g., Thrombosis, Dissection, Embolism, Stent Thrombosis, Rupture).
Pump failure or systemic circulatory instability (e.g., Heart Failure, Cardiogenic Shock, Hemodynamic AE).
Residual cardiovascular events not captured above (e.g., Pericarditis, Chest Pain, Death, Stroke).
New onset or trial-related events affecting the brain, spinal cord, nerves, and mental health (e.g., Stroke, Headache, Seizure). Excludes baseline neurological conditions.
Events involving blood flow disruption or vascular injury to the brain (e.g., Stroke, TIA, Infarction).
Convulsive activity and epileptic conditions resulting from abnormal electrical activity (e.g., Seizure, Convulsion, Epilepsy).
Functional impairments affecting movement, sensation, coordination, or nerve conduction excluding vascular causes (e.g., Paralysis, Neuropathy, Weakness, Tremor).
Alterations in consciousness, cognition, mood, or behavior (e.g., Delirium, Depression, Encephalopathy, Psychomotor).
Remaining neurological adverse events including headaches, infections, structural abnormalities, and inflammatory conditions.
New onset or trial-related events affecting the digestive system, liver, and biliary tract (e.g., Nausea, Vomiting, Diarrhea, Ulcer). Excludes baseline GI conditions.
Active bleeding or hemorrhage within the GI tract (e.g., UGI bleed, Hematochezia)
Disorders of movement, secretion, or sensation (e.g., Nausea, Vomiting, Diarrhea, Constipation, Pain, Bloating)
Inflammatory, infectious, or mucosal damage conditions (e.g., Gastritis, Colitis, Pancreatitis, Ulcers)
Mechanical integrity failures or obstructions (e.g., Perforation, Fistula, Obstruction, Gangrene)
Unclassified GI events, vascular issues, ascites, or non-matching adverse events
New onset or trial-related events affecting bones, joints, muscles, and connective tissue (e.g., Fracture, Arthritis, Back Pain). Excludes baseline musculoskeletal conditions.
Bone breaks including pathological, traumatic, and site-specific fractures.
Symptomatic reports of discomfort, ache, or pain without confirmed structural diagnosis.
Pathologies affecting muscle function and tendon integrity (e.g., myopathy, spasm, tendinosis).
Inflammation, swelling, or structural issues of joints and adjacent soft tissue.
Residual MSK events including deformities, mobility issues, and complex outcomes.
New onset events caused by infectious agents or pathogens (e.g., Sepsis, Pneumonia, UTI). Excludes baseline infectious conditions.
Systemic infections involving the blood or resulting in septic shock (e.g., Sepsis, Bacteremia, Candidemia).
Infections localized to skin, soft tissue, wounds, or surgical/device sites (e.g., Cellulitis, Abscess, Catheter, Incision).
Infections affecting the upper or lower respiratory tract and ENT structures (e.g., Pneumonia, Influenza, URI).
Miscellaneous or unspecified infections not fitting above categories, including pathogen-specific classifications.
New onset or trial-related events affecting the lungs, airways, and breathing (e.g., Respiratory Failure, Dyspnea). Excludes baseline respiratory conditions.
New onset events related to blood disorders, coagulation, and blood counts (e.g., Hemorrhage, Thrombocytopenia). Excludes baseline hematologic conditions.
Events characterized by blood loss, hemorrhage, hematoma, or vascular leakage.
Events involving abnormal clotting, embolism, vessel occlusion, or obstruction.
Abnormalities in blood cell counts, types, or function including anemia and cytopenias.
Adverse events specifically resulting from blood product administration.
Hematologic adverse events not fitting specific mechanisms or unclassified endpoints.
New onset or trial-related events affecting the skin and underlying tissue (e.g., Rash, Hematoma). Excludes baseline dermatological conditions.
Inflammatory, allergic, or immune-mediated skin reactions characterized by redness, itching, or eruption (e.g., drug eruption, urticaria, pruritus).
Adverse events localized to injection, implant, incision, catheter, or device sites (e.g., pain, hematoma, extravasation, dehiscence).
Structural abnormalities and fluid accumulations not strictly tied to a procedural wound (e.g., cysts, lumps, lymphedema, edema, seroma).
Loss of skin integrity, necrosis, bleeding, or specific surface abnormalities (e.g., ulcers, necrotizing fasciitis, petechiae, skin hemorrhage).
Unspecified skin conditions, mucosal inflammation, or miscellaneous symptoms not fitting primary structural categories.

New onset or trial-related events related to metabolism, electrolytes, kidney function, and abnormal laboratory findings (e.g., Renal Failure, Elevated Enzymes). Excludes baseline metabolic conditions.
New onset events related to benign or malignant tumors and cancer (e.g., Carcinoma, Metastasis). Excludes baseline cancer diagnoses.
New onset non-specific systemic symptoms, administration site conditions, and vital outcomes not tied to a specific organ system (e.g., Fatigue, Pain, Injection Site Reaction, Death).
Non-localized physiological disturbances affecting whole-body status such as fatigue, temperature, or weight.
Critical life-status events including mortality, late death, and shock states.
Generalized or non-organ-specific pain sensations and discomfort levels.
Catch-all for remaining general disorders not fitting primary buckets, including allergies and lab abnormalities.
Adverse events that do not fit into the specified system organ classes or are unclassifiable.
Conditions affecting the eye and visual apparatus not covered by neurological or skin categories.
Disorders affecting reproductive organs and urinary tract structures, excluding neoplasms and renal metabolic issues.
Adverse events resulting from external forces, physical trauma, accidents, assault, or environmental exposure.
Unclassifiable adverse events, general descriptors, definitions, or rare conditions not fitting specific subcategories.
Substances administered to participants, including drugs, biologics, placebos, supplements, fluids, and radiopharmaceuticals.
Medical hardware, implants, instruments, or equipment used, implanted, or provided to participants as treatment.
Intravascular scaffolds including bare-metal, drug-eluting, and bioresorbable varieties used for arterial support.
Interventional delivery tools, dilatation balloons, aspiration catheters, and closure devices.
Internal structural replacements, active assist devices, and prosthetics such as joint replacements, occluders, and LVADs.
Diagnostic equipment, intraoperative visualization, external monitoring systems, and respiratory support devices.
Catch-all for unspecified devices, software, wearables, wound care, and non-fitting interventions.
Surgeries, invasive techniques, clinical actions, or interventional methods performed by healthcare providers.
Open surgical procedures involving the heart and great vessels, including bypass, valve replacement, and transplant.
Minimally invasive catheter-based procedures for coronary or vascular treatment, such as PCI, angioplasty, and stenting.
Invasive surgical procedures outside the cardiovascular system, including orthopedics, ENT, soft tissue, and non-cardiac vascular surgeries.
Procedural diagnostic actions primarily for visualization or functional measurement, such as angiography, colonoscopy, manometry, and guided imaging.
Catch-all for unspecified procedures, supportive care, resuscitation, access routes, or device insertions not covered by therapeutic or diagnostic categories.
Non-pharmaceutical, non-device therapies involving patient behavior, lifestyle modifications, education, counseling, or psychological interventions.
Interventions that do not fit into the above categories, unspecified interventions, or administrative items.
Details regarding participant assignment, treatment arms, blinding, or randomization methods.
Inclusion/exclusion criteria, patient selection requirements, demographic thresholds, or staging requirements for participation.
Specific planned procedures, dosing schedules, intervention descriptions, measurement definitions, endpoint definitions, and visit timing.
Specific medical interventions, surgical techniques, device usage, dosing administration, and therapeutic actions planned in the protocol.
Definitions of primary/secondary outcomes, event adjudication criteria, scoring algorithms, measurement specifications, and standards.
Visit schedules, dosing intervals, observation periods, follow-up windows, procedure durations, and time-based demarcations.
Rules regarding compliance, deviations, violations, stopping criteria, non-adherence records, and reasons for non-conformance.
Miscellaneous protocol details, statistical analysis plans, general notes, or study design elements not fitting specific functional categories.
Dynamic execution and administrative events including participant withdrawals, discontinuations, adherence, compliance, protocol deviations, missed visits, and site closures.
Events where participants discontinue, withdraw consent, refuse treatment, or meet withdrawal criteria.
Administrative, logistical, or site-level events including closures, supply issues, holds, and sponsor directives.
Subject adherence to prescribed regimens, medication intake, and scheduled study visits (including missed appointments).
Errors in study execution involving incorrect procedures, data collection failures, or administration errors.
Unclassified operational text, data analysis notes, or administrative details not fitting specific event types.
Administrative notes, definitions, missing data, or miscellaneous content not fitting other specific categories (e.g., Titles, vague terms, general population descriptions).
Baseline malignant and benign neoplasms, cancers, and tumors (e.g., Lung cancer, Lymphoma). Excludes new onset tumors.
Invasive carcinomas, sarcomas, and solid tumors across all organ systems including CNS
Cancers of the blood, bone marrow, and lymphatic system (e.g., Leukemia, Lymphoma)
Non-malignant growths including adenomas, polyps, and hyperplasia
Precancerous conditions such as dysplasia and carcinoma in situ
Unspecified, rare, or mixed oncological conditions not fitting primary pathological groups
Baseline conditions affecting bones, muscles, joints, and connective tissue (e.g., Arthritis). Excludes new onset events.
Baseline conditions affecting metabolism, hormones, and biochemical processes (e.g., Diabetes, Lipid disorders). Excludes new onset events.
Baseline disorders of the kidney, bladder, urinary system, and reproductive organs (e.g., Renal failure, Kidney stones). Excludes new onset events.
Conditions not fitting into the above systems, mixed, unspecified diagnoses, or non-condition states.
Study endpoints, efficacy metrics, and composite health occurrences (e.g., MACE, Survival). Excludes specific event names (which belong to adverse_events).
Aggregated efficacy metrics combining multiple clinical events (e.g., MACE, MACCE, TLF).
Continuous measurements derived from imaging, biomarkers, or disease activity scores.
Miscellaneous endpoints including functional status, device performance, or undefined metrics.
Endpoints focused on harm monitoring, adverse event incidence, tolerability, or treatment discontinuation due to safety.
Continuous or ordinal biological, physical, or laboratory measurements (e.g., Lab Values, Imaging metrics, Physiological parameters).
Quantitative structural dimensions, volumes, and metrics derived from medical imaging.
Vital signs, hemodynamics, anthropometrics, and functional capacity measurements.
Healthcare consumption metrics related to time, cost, and procedural administration.
Composite scores, survival rates, and miscellaneous quantitative measures not fitting primary modalities.
Subjective assessments of health status, quality of life, symptoms, or functional status measured via scales.
Measures of disease progression, staging, remission, or recurrence status.
Technical performance, duration, adherence, or operational metrics related to the intervention procedure.
Administrative and study flow outcomes including retention rates, withdrawal rates, and protocol adherence metrics.
Outcomes that do not fit into the primary categories, including interventions, administrative text, or ambiguous entries.
Catch-all for unclassifiable samples.
